question.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{3}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{2{x}^{6}+7{x}^{3}-9}{2{x}^{3}-1} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{2{x}^{6}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{7{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{9}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(2{x}^{3}+7-\frac{9}{{x}^{3}})}{(2-\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{2{x}^{3}+7-0}{2-0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{lim}_{x\to \infty }(2{x}^{3}+7) \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
